design.actions: an ACTION is (module, callable, witness, shape): call it, record the observable. The witness comes from the environment's OWN vocabulary (string literals in the module) plus neutral tokens, in both the scalar and the element shape (round 5 measured that a str is not a list).
design.kind_taxonomy: REMOVED / NOW_RAISES / NO_LONGER_RAISES / VALUE_CHANGED / OTHER -- never added together.
design.learned_vs_held_out: witnesses are split by a fixed rule -- even positions learned, odd held out -- so the check's blindness is a property of the module, not of a seed.
design.minor_bump_regime: one real MINOR bump (packaging 24.0 -> 24.1) is reported apart, because 2026 measurements put 33.8% of patch and 64.4% of minor releases at carrying a semantic break.
design.nondeterminism_control: the old tree is executed TWICE; anything that differs at the SAME revision is excluded and named, so randomness cannot be reported as an environment change.
design.per_witness_risk: for every moved action, the fraction of single learned witnesses that would have seen it. That is the risk of 'learn it once', because one experience is one witness.

the_question: Of the learned actions a real environment actually MOVED, what fraction does a check built from experience fail to see? Permanence is a multiplier on the check (the tree's own PERMANENCE_AMPLIFIES_THE_CHECK_KNOWN_COUNTEREXAMPLE); this measures the multiplier on real code.
what_this_shows: On real libraries the environment DOES invalidate learned actions -- 13 of the 42 observable actions (31%) were moved between the tree's own pinned releases -- and 5 were REMOVED, 6 NOW_RAISE, 2 CHANGED VALUE. But every one of the 13 was visible at EVERY single learned witness (per-witness blind risk 0.0; 0 of 13 moves had a blind single witness), and the real minor bump (packaging 24.0 -> 24.1) moved NOTHING at the behaviour level. So on this corpus permanence fails LOUDLY where it is learnable. The danger is elsewhere: 30 of 76 actions (39%) could not be exercised at all with witness arguments, and 4 more read the host environment and are nondeterministic. The blind class is not 'learned and silently wrong'; it is 'never learnable from these observables'. That is the same conclusion the tree's vocabulary-insufficiency certificate states, now with a count.
what_would_falsify_this_reading: A semantic change that keeps the signature, keeps every learned witness identical, and moves a held-out witness: that case exists in the design (BLIND) and occurred 0 times here. It is the class the literature says dominates minor releases; my witnesses cannot reach the domain-valid inputs that would expose it, which is exactly why the 39% unobservable set is the honest place to look next, not a place to celebrate.
